problem:
$$
{a}_{1}=[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 1 \\ 0\end{aligned}],\,{a}_{2}=[\begin{aligned}7 \\ -4 \\ 1\end{aligned}],\,{a}_{3}=[\begin{aligned}10 \\ -5 \\ -14\end{aligned}],\,B={[\begin{aligned}| \\ {v}_{1} \\ |\end{aligned}]\,,[\begin{aligned}| \\ {v}_{2} \\ |\end{aligned}]\,,[\begin{aligned}a \\ b \\ c\end{aligned}]}
$$

Suppose that $V=\text{Span}{{a}_{1},{a}_{2},{a}_{3}}.$ Given that $B$ is an orthogonal basis for $V,$ and that $B$ is derived from $V$ using the Gram-Schmidt process, what is the value of $\frac{a}{b}?$
worked_solution:
We find an orthogonal basis $B$ of $V$ using the Gram-Schmidt process, as follows:

**Step 1.** We set ${v}_{1}={a}_{1}=[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 1 \\ 0\end{aligned}].$

**Step 2.** We find the vector ${v}_{2}$ orthogonal to $\text{Span}{{v}_{1}}$ using the usual formula:

$$
\begin{aligned}{v}_{2} & ={a}_{2}-{\text{proj}}_{{v}_{1}}{a}_{2} \\  & ={a}_{2}-\frac{{a}_{2}\cdot {v}_{1}}{{v}_{1}\cdot {v}_{1}}{v}_{1} \\  & =[\begin{aligned}7 \\ -4 \\ 1\end{aligned}]-\frac{10}{5}[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 1 \\ 0\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}3 \\ -6 \\ 1\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

**Step 3.** We find the vector ${v}_{3}$ orthogonal to $\text{Span}{{v}_{1},{v}_{2}}$ using the usual formula:

$$
\begin{aligned}{v}_{3} & ={a}_{3}-{\text{proj}}_{{v}_{1}}\,{a}_{3}-{\text{proj}}_{{v}_{2}}\,{a}_{3} \\  & ={a}_{3}-\frac{{a}_{3}\cdot {v}_{1}}{{v}_{1}\cdot {v}_{1}}{v}_{1}-\frac{{a}_{3}\cdot {v}_{2}}{{v}_{2}\cdot {v}_{2}}{v}_{2} \\  & =[\begin{aligned}10 \\ -5 \\ -14\end{aligned}]-\frac{15}{5}[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 1 \\ 0\end{aligned}]-\frac{46}{46}[\begin{aligned}3 \\ -6 \\ 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}10 \\ -5 \\ -14\end{aligned}]-3[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 1 \\ 0\end{aligned}]-[\begin{aligned}3 \\ -6 \\ 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}1 \\ -2 \\ -15\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, $a=1,$ $b=-2,$ and $\frac{a}{b}=-\frac{1}{2}.$
